issues.t: High-voltage battery modules can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. Some owners see a battery warning, lose range, or are told by the dealer to limit charging to 80% until the repair is done. In rare cases a module can overheat, smoke or catch fire.
issues.why: Some cells in certain high-voltage battery modules slowly discharge themselves, which can lead to overheating. Audi recalled 2019-2022 e-tron and e-tron Sportback models, added monitoring software and replaces bad modules.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov or with an Audi dealer. Until the work is done, follow Audi's charging limit and park outside if the dealer tells you to. The repair is free.

issues.t: Coolant leaks into front electric motor
issues.sym: An 'electrical system malfunction' or drive-system warning appears, power drops, and the car may coast to a stop or refuse to move. Some owners notice the coolant level falling beforehand.
issues.why: Coolant from the cooling circuit can seep past a seal into the front electric motor, shorting it out. Owners report the motor and related parts being replaced, sometimes for weeks.
issues.next: If the warning appears, pull over safely and have the car towed to an Audi dealer. Ask whether it is covered by the 8-year/100,000-mile high-voltage warranty or the new-car warranty.

issues.t: Sudden loss of drive power with electrical malfunction warning
issues.sym: While driving, warnings such as 'Electrical system malfunction - stop safely' appear, and the car loses power, goes into a limp mode or shuts down, sometimes at highway speed or in an intersection.
issues.why: Faults in the drive motors, the main drive controller or the high-voltage system trigger a safety shutdown. Owners report front motors, controllers and other high-voltage parts being replaced.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Get safely off the road and turn on your hazards. Have the car towed to a dealer and ask for all stored fault codes to be read and any software updates to be installed.

issues.t: Brake pedal can come loose from the brake booster (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. If the fastener fails, the brake pedal can separate from the brake booster and the brakes will not work when you press the pedal.
issues.why: The fastener that joins the brake pedal to the brake booster may not have been assembled correctly at the factory.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls and book the free inspection and repair at an Audi dealer as soon as possible.

issues.t: 240-volt portable charging cable can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: When charging at home with the compact 240-volt cord plugged into a wall outlet, the plug, outlet or cable can get hot, smell burnt or melt, especially when charging to 100%.
issues.why: With some home outlets, the plug end of the 240-volt portable charging cable can overheat under a long, full charge.
issues.next: Stop using the 240-volt portable cord until Audi gives you the replacement cable with a temperature sensor. Use the 120-volt cord, a wall-mounted charger or public chargers instead.

issues.t: Water can enter battery through charging socket seal (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before failure. Water can get past the charge port seal into the high-voltage battery area, which can lead to a short circuit, warning messages or a fire.
issues.why: A faulty seal at the charging socket could let moisture into the high-voltage battery system.
issues.next: Make sure the recall was done on your car. Dealers install a new seal and replace damaged parts for free.

issues.t: Brake booster weld defect reduces braking assist (recall)
issues.sym: Brake and stability warnings light up, the pedal may feel harder, and ABS and stability control may stop working.
issues.why: A poorly welded rotor and shaft inside the electric brake booster can separate.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for this recall and have the dealer replace the brake booster for free.

issues.t: Brake booster corrosion can disable ABS and stability control (recall)
issues.sym: Warnings for ABS, stability control or brakes appear, and the speedometer display may stop working. Brake assist may be reduced.
issues.why: Corrosion inside the brake booster can cause it to fail, taking the ABS, stability control and brake assist with it.
issues.next: Have the free recall done at an Audi dealer, which replaces the brake booster.

issues.t: Dead 12-volt battery, car won't wake up or start
issues.sym: The car won't unlock, the screens stay dark, or it won't go into Ready mode. It may happen after the car sits, or after DC fast charging.
issues.why: The small 12-volt battery runs the car's computers. It can run down from modules that stay awake, software faults, or a charging fault, and Audi has issued service bulletins on drained 12-volt batteries and no-starts.
issues.next: Try a jump start or a 12-volt battery charger. If it keeps happening, have the dealer test the 12-volt battery and check for software updates and bulletins about battery drain.

issues.t: Car won't charge or charge port won't release the cable
issues.sym: Charging won't start or stops part way, the charge flap won't open or close, or the cable stays locked in the port.
issues.why: Problems with the charge port, its locking actuator, the charge flap or the charging software. Audi has released bulletins and software for charging faults and for checking charge socket parts.
issues.next: Try another charger and make sure the car is unlocked. Use the emergency release for the cable if needed. Have the dealer check for charging software updates and charge port faults.

issues.t: Low coolant warning or coolant leak
issues.sym: A low coolant warning appears, sometimes even though the reservoir looks full. Some cars lose coolant and leave a sweet-smelling puddle.
issues.why: Audi issued bulletins for false low-coolant warnings and for leaks from an electric coolant valve. Some cars were also filled with the wrong type of coolant at the factory.
issues.next: Check the reservoir when the car is cold. Don't top up with ordinary coolant; e-tron needs a specific Audi coolant. Have the dealer check for leaks and bulletins.

issues.t: Air suspension fault warning or car sitting low
issues.sym: An air suspension malfunction message appears, the car sits lower at one corner, or the ride height won't change.
issues.why: Leaking air struts, a weak compressor or suspension control unit faults. Audi has issued bulletins for air suspension warnings and suspension control unit fault codes.
issues.next: Have it checked soon, because a leaking strut overworks the compressor. Ask the dealer about software updates before replacing parts.

issues.t: Clunk or rattle from rear axle over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk, rumble or rattle from the back of the car when driving over bumps or rough roads.
issues.why: Audi issued several bulletins for rear axle and rear suspension noises, including loose or worn parts in the rear axle area.
issues.next: Have the dealer road test the car and check the rear suspension bulletins. It is usually not urgent, but have it inspected.

issues.t: Squeak or creak from front suspension
issues.sym: A squeak or creak from the front while driving, often over bumps or when turning at low speed.
issues.why: Audi issued bulletins for front suspension noises, including replacing a drive link shaft for front-end rumbling or squeaks.
issues.next: Mention the noise during a service visit and ask the dealer to check the front suspension bulletins.

issues.t: Sunroof or roof water leaks into cabin
issues.sym: Wet carpets or footwells, water dripping from the headliner, or damp electronics after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water gets past the panoramic roof seals or its drains, or other body seals. Owners worry about water reaching electrical parts.
issues.next: Dry the interior quickly and have the dealer test the roof seals and clear the drains. Water can damage electronics if ignored.

issues.t: Infotainment unit fails and rear camera goes dark (recall)
issues.sym: The main screen goes blank after the car has been shut off, and the rearview camera image doesn't show when reversing.
issues.why: The infotainment main unit can be damaged internally when the vehicle is switched off.
issues.next: Check for this recall. The dealer replaces the infotainment main unit for free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not appear, software fault (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the rear camera picture doesn't show up correctly or at all.
issues.why: A software error can stop the rearview camera image from displaying. Audi issued a recall in 2025 that covers e-tron models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free software update done. Until then, use your mirrors and look behind you.

issues.t: Rearview camera shows black screen (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the screen stays black or blank instead of showing the camera view.
issues.why: An infotainment software fault can stop the rear camera image from appearing.
issues.next: Have the free software update done at an Audi dealer. Until then, check your mirrors and look behind you when reversing.

issues.t: Screens or virtual cockpit go blank or flicker
issues.sym: The driver display or center screens flicker, show lines or go black while driving, sometimes taking climate controls with them.
issues.why: Software and hardware faults in the displays and infotainment modules. Audi issued a bulletin for flickering lines in the virtual cockpit, and owners report cluster replacements.
issues.next: Restarting the car may bring the screens back. Have the dealer check for software updates and fault codes.

issues.t: No sound from audio system
issues.sym: No sound at all from the radio, media or phone calls, even though the screen works.
issues.why: On certain early-production 2019 e-trons, an electronics control module for the audio system fails. Audi issued a bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check the bulletin for the audio electronics module.

issues.t: Battery module controller (SX6) failure
issues.sym: High-voltage battery warnings, the car won't charge or drive, and the dealer says battery control modules on top of the battery must be replaced.
issues.why: The control units mounted on the high-voltage battery fail. An owner linked it to coolant getting into high-voltage parts; outside warranty it is a major repair.
issues.next: Check whether you are still within the 8-year/100,000-mile high-voltage warranty before paying for the repair.

issues.t: Car rolls on hills even in gear
issues.sym: The car rolls backward or forward on a slope after stopping, even in Drive or Reverse, or the brake hold doesn't hold.
issues.why: Owners report the hold features not keeping the car still on inclines. Electric cars don't creep or hold like a regular automatic unless the hold function works.
issues.next: Use the brake pedal and parking brake on hills. Report it to the dealer and ask for a software check.

issues.t: Red steering warning light
issues.sym: A red steering warning appears and steering may feel heavier.
issues.why: Audi issued bulletins for steering warnings tied to specific fault codes in the steering system.
issues.next: If steering feels heavy, stop safely. Have the dealer read the codes and check the steering bulletins.

issues.t: Glove box hinge pin can block knee airbag (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. In a crash the knee airbag may not deploy correctly.
issues.why: A glove box hinge pin may not be secured, letting the lid trim get in the way of the knee airbag.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and secure the hinge pin for free.

issues.t: Rear seat belt may not hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: The middle rear seat belt may stop locking, so a child seat installed with the belt can loosen.
issues.why: The automatic locking feature of the rear seat belt retractor can switch off too early.
issues.next: Use the LATCH anchors for child seats until the dealer inspects and replaces the belt for free.

issues.t: Brake line connection can leak fluid (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leak, a brake warning light, or a softer brake pedal and longer stops.
issues.why: A brake line fitting may have been overtightened at the factory and can fail.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check for this recall on 2024 Q8 e-tron models. The dealer inspects and replaces the line for free.
